zh: 删除之后剩下的字母保持原来的相对顺序，所以保留下来的部分就是原串的一个非降子序列；删得最少等价于留得最多。
答案是 |S| 减去最长非降子序列的长度。注意是“非降”，相同字母可以都保留。
维护数组 tails，第 i 项表示长度为 i+1 的非降子序列最小可能的结尾字母。对每个字母，找第一个严格大于它的位置（upper_bound）替换；找不到就追加到末尾。最后输出 |S| 减去 tails 的长度。
en: The remaining letters keep their original order, so the kept part is a non-decreasing subsequence of the word; deleting as few as possible means keeping as many as possible.
The answer is |S| minus the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence. It is non-decreasing, so equal letters may all be kept.

Maintain an array tails whose entry i is the smallest possible last letter of a non-decreasing subsequence of length i+1. For each letter, find the first entry strictly greater than it (upper_bound) and replace it, or append the letter if there is none. Print |S| minus the length of tails.

explanationEn:
## Approach

The kept letters must form a subsequence of the original string that is lexicographically non-decreasing. Let L be the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence; then at most L letters can be kept, and the answer is `n-L`. Use tails to maintain the smallest ending character of a non-decreasing subsequence of each length; for each character, use upper_bound to find the first position greater than it and replace it, or otherwise extend the sequence.

## Correctness

Every way of keeping letters is a non-decreasing subsequence of the original string, so its length is at most L and at least n−L characters must be deleted. Conversely, the longest non-decreasing subsequence itself is obtained by deleting all the other characters, so deleting n−L characters suffices. The upper_bound update of tails is the classic longest non-decreasing subsequence algorithm; repeated letters can extend the sequence, and the final length is exactly L.

## Complexity

Time O(n log n), space O(n).
